hypothesis: The ContinuedFraction.evaluate method is too aggressive in throwing a ConvergenceException when it encounters NaN or Infinity during intermediate calculations. In many numerical contexts, especially with large inputs, these values can be transient or represent a limit that should be handled more gracefully (e.g., by capping the value or using a more stable approximation) rather than aborting the entire calculation.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying the ContinuedFraction.evaluate method to handle these numerical instabilities (NaN/Infinity) by either using a fallback value or adjusting the iteration logic to avoid the divergence, rather than throwing an exception.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace and code snippet confirm that the failure is a direct result of an explicit check for NaN/Infinity in the iterative evaluation loop, which is a procedural/algorithmic choice for handling numerical divergence.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an algorithmic limitation in how the continued fraction evaluation handles numerical instability. It is not a missing check (Checking) because the check exists and is causing the failure; it is not an initialization error (Assignment/Initialization) because the values are being computed correctly according to the current algorithm; it is not a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object) because the functionality exists but is numerically fragile.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The check is present and functioning as written; the issue is that the algorithm itself is not robust enough to handle the numerical conditions it encounters.
